subject.title: fix(sessions): suppress terminal transcript gate for sessions still fresh under reset policy (fixes #106403)

question: Should reset-policy freshness override the terminal transcript reconciliation gate across every session-resolution path, or should the unconditional gate remain while transcript writers restore the registry timestamp invariant?
rationale: The choice trades false context-destroying rollovers against the gate's intended recovery of terminal rows whose transcript changed after registry completion; source inspection alone cannot establish which invariant maintainers want authoritative.

options.title: Adopt freshness-first consistently
options.body: Make reset-policy freshness authoritative in both auto-reply and command resolution, retaining the transcript gate only for policy-stale entries and proving both outcomes.

options.title: Restore the writer invariant
options.body: Keep the unconditional reconciliation gate and update every managed post-run transcript writer to advance the canonical registry timestamp, with regression coverage for late writes.

options.title: Pause this behavioral change
options.body: Leave the current gate unchanged until the terminal-row recovery contract can be redesigned without creating entry-point divergence.

recommendation.title: Adopt freshness-first consistently
recommendation.body: Make reset-policy freshness authoritative in both auto-reply and command resolution, retaining the transcript gate only for policy-stale entries and proving both outcomes.
